title: Power-Building: Hypertrophy Block
subtitle: 12 weeks, 7 sessions per week, main lifts at a set percentage of your 1RM
summary: The mainly-hypertrophy half of the power-building plan: Legs, Push, Pull, Legs, Push, Pull and Arms, with the squat, incline bench, rows and RDL taken at 80%, then 75%, then 70% of your 1RM. Sets step up each week while accessory work steps down, so total volume stays constant.
progressionNotes: Stick to the given RIR and percentage: weeks 1-4 at 80% of your 1RM, weeks 5-8 at 75% and weeks 9-12 at 70%. Each week inside a block adds sets on the main lifts; RIR goes 3-4, 2, 1, 0.

guide.heading: How the block is built
body: This is the mainly-hypertrophy block: 12 weeks. Weeks 1-4 use 8 working sets with the main lifts at 80% of your 1RM, weeks 5-8 use 12 working sets at 75%, and weeks 9-12 use 15 working sets at 70%.

Inside each 4-week block your effort ramps up: Week 1 at 3-4 RIR, Week 2 at 2 RIR, Week 3 at 1 RIR, Week 4 at 0 RIR. You must stick to the RIR and the percentages, otherwise you will get fatigued very quickly.
The last week of each block adds an AMRAP set on the main lifts.

guide.heading: Your split calendar
body: The split runs on a 10-day cycle: Legs, Push, Pull, Rest, Legs, Push, Pull, Rest, Arms, Rest. That is 7 sessions per program week.
The app assigns sessions to your training days in order, so the week counter follows sessions rather than the calendar.

guide.heading: Main lifts: the progression
body: Weeks 1-4 (80% 1RM): squat, incline bench, rows and RDL go 3x6, 4x5, 5x6 (squat 5x5), then 5x5 plus an AMRAP set.
Weeks 5-8 (75% 1RM): 3x8, 4x8, 5x8, then 5x8 plus an AMRAP set.
Weeks 9-12 (70% 1RM): 3x10, 4x10, 5x10, then 5x10 plus an AMRAP set.

guide.heading: Volume management
body: If you do not think 5 sets of incline bench press is worth it when your maximum volume for that day on chest is 5, you can opt to do a lower version, for example 3 sets. Just stay with the given weight and RIR.
Reach each weekly set goal across the week. For example, do 10 sets of chest on the first push day and 5 on the second.
As you gain experience, auto-adjust your working sets.

guide.heading: Rest between sets
body: Rest 3-4 minutes on the big compound lift, then 2 minutes for the rest.

guide.heading: After the block
body: Follow it with the Strength Block (4 weeks, then a deload). For the accessory work in the Strength Block, repeat one of your favorite workouts from the 8 working set mesocycle.

guide.heading: Training techniques used
body: RP = Rest-pause: after you reach technical failure, wait 10-15 seconds and squeeze out some more reps.
P = Long-length partials: partial reps with the target muscle at its lengthened position, at the end of a movement such as the bottom of a curl, the top of a pulldown or the bottom of a bench press.
S = Intra-set stretch: after you finish your set, stretch that muscle for 35 seconds.
Superset: do the two exercises back to back, then rest.

guide.heading: Terms
body: RIR = reps in reserve. If a set says 3 RIR, pick a weight and stop at a rep where you feel you could still push out 3 more reps.
%1RM = percentage of your one-rep max. For 80%, take 80% of your one-rep max and use that weight.
